details.description: Bacterial spot is a damaging disease of peaches that affects leaves, twigs, and fruit. It often leads to severe defoliation, which weakens the tree and reduces the size and quality of the fruit. The bacteria are easily spread by wind-driven rain during warm weather.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots on leaves that turn deep purple to black
Centers of leaf spots drop out, leaving a 'shot-hole' appearance
Deep, pitted, dark lesions on the skin of the fruit
Yellowing and severe dropping of infected leaves
causes: Bacteria overwintering in twig cankers and buds
Splashing rain and high winds spreading bacteria to new growth
Warm temperatures combined with high surface moisture
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides during early spring/bud break
Apply oxytetracycline or other labeled bactericides during the growing season if pressure is high
Maintain optimal tree nutrition to help trees withstand defoliation stress
prevention: Plant peach varieties that are highly resistant to bacterial spot
Prune out visible twig cankers during the dormant season
Plant windbreaks around the orchard to reduce wind-driven rain spread
Ensure good airflow through the canopy via proper pruning
details.recommended_action: Apply a labeled copper or antibiotic spray, and ensure proper orchard airflow.

weather_advisory.message: Current weather conditions are not favorable for disease spread.
